title: Proof
body_md:
($\Rightarrow$) 
Fix $d$ with $\|d\|=1$. For any $t \geq 0$ and $\lambda \in [0,1]$, define $x = \overline{x} + td$. Then,
\begin{align*}
 \varphi_d ((1-\lambda)t) & = h (\overline{x} + (1-\lambda) td) = h(\lambda \overline{x} + (1-\lambda)(\overline{x} + td)) = h(\lambda \overline{x} + (1-\lambda) x).
\end{align*}
Applying the $(\rho,\gamma)$-weak quasar-convexity of $h$ at $\overline{x}$ and since $\|x - \overline{x}\| = \|td\| = t$, we get
\begin{align*}
h\bigl(\lambda \overline{x} + (1-\lambda)x\bigr) 
&\leq \gamma\lambda  h(\overline{x}) + (1 - \gamma\lambda)  h(x) 
   + \tfrac{\gamma\rho}{2}  \lambda\left(1 - \tfrac{\lambda}{2-\gamma}\right) \|x - \overline{x}\|^2 \\
&= \gamma\lambda  \varphi_d(0) + (1 - \gamma\lambda)  \varphi_d(t) 
   + \tfrac{\gamma\rho}{2}  \lambda\left(1 - \tfrac{\lambda}{2-\gamma}\right) t^2,
\end{align*}
i.e., \eqref{1d:char} holds.

\noindent
($\Leftarrow$) 
Let $x \in \mathbb{R}^n$ be arbitrary. If $x = \overline{x}$, the weak quasar-convexity inequality holds trivially (both sides equal $h(\overline{x})$). Otherwise, define
$d = \tfrac{x - \overline{x}}{\|x - \overline{x}\|}$ and $t = \|x - \overline{x}\| > 0$,
hence $\|d\| = 1$ and $x = \overline{x} + td$. Then, for any $\lambda \in [0,1]$,
\begin{align*}
h\bigl(\lambda \overline{x} + (1-\lambda)x\bigr) 
&= h\bigl(\overline{x} + (1-\lambda)td\bigr) = \varphi_d\bigl((1-\lambda)t\bigr).
\end{align*}
Applying relation \eqref{1d:char} to $\varphi_d$ gives
\begin{align*}
\varphi_d\bigl((1-\lambda)t\bigr) 
&\leq \gamma\lambda  \varphi_d(0) + (1 - \gamma\lambda)  \varphi_d(t) 
   + \tfrac{\gamma\rho}{2}  \lambda\left(1 - \tfrac{\lambda}{2-\gamma}\right) t^2 \\
&= \gamma\lambda  h(\overline{x}) + (1 - \gamma\lambda)  h(x) 
   + \tfrac{\gamma\rho}{2}  \lambda\left(1 - \tfrac{\lambda}{2-\gamma}\right) \|x - \overline{x}\|^2,
\end{align*}
i.e., $h$ is $(\rho,\gamma)$-weakly quasar-convex at $\overline{x}$.

label: prop:quasar-sum
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:quasar-sum}
Let $h_i: \mathbb{R}^n \to \mathbb{R}$ be $(\rho_i,\gamma)$-weakly quasar-convex with respect to $\overline{x} \in \operatorname{argmin}_{\mathbb{R}^{n}}h_i$ for every $i=1,\cdots,m$, where $\gamma \in   ]0, 1]$ is the same for all $i$. Then for every $\alpha_i \geq 0$, the function
$h := \sum_{i=1}^m \alpha_i h_i$ 
is $\left(\sum_{i=1}^m \alpha_i \rho_i,\gamma\right)$-weakly quasar-convex with respect to $\overline{x}$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Since $\overline{x} \in \cap_{i} \operatorname{argmin}_{\mathbb{R}^{n}}h_i$ and $\alpha_i \geq 0$, it follows that $\overline{x} \in \operatorname{argmin}_{\mathbb{R}^n} h$. Then for every $x \in \mathbb{R}^n$ and every $\lambda \in [0,1]$, we have
\begin{align*}
h\bigl(\lambda \overline{x} + (1-\lambda)x\bigr) 
&= \sum_{i=1}^m \alpha_i  h_i\bigl(\lambda \overline{x} + (1-\lambda)x\bigr) \\
&\leq \sum_{i=1}^m \alpha_i \Biggl(  \gamma\lambda  h_i (\overline{x}) + (1 - \gamma\lambda) h_i(x) + \tfrac{\gamma \rho_i}{2}  \lambda \left(1 - \tfrac{ \lambda }{2 - \gamma}\right) \|x - \overline{x}\|^2 \Biggr) \\
&= \gamma\lambda \sum_{i=1}^m \alpha_i h_i(\overline{x}) + (1 - \gamma\lambda) \sum_{i=1}^m \alpha_i h_i(x)  + \tfrac{\gamma}{2}  \lambda\left(1 - \tfrac{\lambda}{2-\gamma}\right) \|x - \overline{x} \|^2 \sum_{i=1}^m \alpha_i \rho_i \\
& = \gamma\lambda  h(\overline{x}) + (1 - \gamma \lambda)  h(x) + \tfrac{\gamma}{2} \left( \sum_{i=1}^m \alpha_i \rho_i\right) \lambda \left(1 - \tfrac{\lambda}{2-\gamma}\right) \|x - \overline{x} \|^2.
\end{align*}
Therefore, $h$ is $(\rho,\gamma)$-weakly quasar-convex at $\overline{x}$ with modulus $\rho = \sum_{i=1}^m \alpha_i \rho_i$ and $\gamma \in ]0, 1]$.

body_md:
\label{prop:quasar-composition}
Let $h: \mathbb{R}^m \to \mathbb{R}$ be $(\rho, \gamma)$-weakly quasar-convex with respect to $\overline{y} \in \operatorname{argmin} h$, with $\rho\geq 0$ and $\gamma \in ]0, 1]$. Let $A: \mathbb{R}^n \to \mathbb{R}^m$ be a linear operator satisfying $A\overline{x} = \overline{y}$, and assume $\overline{x} \in \operatorname{argmin}_{\mathbb{R}^n} g$ where $g(x) = h(Ax)$. Then $g$ is $\bigl( \rho \|A\|_{ \mathrm{op}}^2, \gamma \bigr)$-weakly quasar-convex with respect to $\overline{x}$, where $\|A\|_{ \mathrm{op}}$ denotes the operator norm of $A$.

label: lem:moreau-argmin
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:moreau-argmin}
 Let $h$ be proper lower semicontinuous function, and $\overline{x} \in \operatorname{argmin}_{\mathbb{R}^n} h$. Then, for every ${\beta}>0$, $h^{\beta}$ is finite-valued on $\mathbb{R}^n$, $h^{\beta}(\overline{x})=h(\overline{x})$, and $\operatorname{argmin}_{\mathbb{R}^n} h^{\beta} = \operatorname{argmin}_{\mathbb{R}^n} h$.
head: environment

label: prop:moreau-structural
title: Theorem
head: environment
name: Moreau Envelope Preserves Weak Quasar-Convexity

label: eq:near-opt
title: Proof
body_md:
By Lemma~\ref{lem:moreau-argmin} (applied with this particular ${\beta}>0$), $h^{\beta}$ is finite-valued, $h^{\beta}(\overline{x})=h(\overline{x})$, and $\overline{x}\in\operatorname{argmin}_{\mathbb{R}^n} h^{\beta}$. It remains to prove the chord inequality for $h^{\beta}$ with modulus $\rho_{\beta}$.
 
Fix $x\in\mathbb{R}^n$, $\lambda\in[0,1]$, and $\varepsilon>0$. Choose $y^\ast\in\mathbb{R}^n$ with
 
\begin{equation}\label{eq:near-opt}
h(y^\ast)+\tfrac{1}{2{\beta}}\|x-y^\ast\|^2 \leq h^{\beta}(x)+\varepsilon .
\end{equation}
 
Set $z_\lambda := \lambda\overline{x}+(1-\lambda)x$ and $y_\lambda := \lambda\overline{x}+(1-\lambda)y^\ast$.
 
Since $y_\lambda$ is feasible for $h^{\beta}(z_\lambda)$ and $z_\lambda-y_\lambda=(1-\lambda)(x-y^\ast)$,
 
\begin{equation}\label{eq:step21}
h^{\beta}(z_\lambda) \leq h(y_\lambda) + \tfrac{(1-\lambda)^2}{2{\beta}}\|x-y^\ast\|^2 .
\end{equation}
 
Applying \eqref{eq:quasar-wconvex} to the pair $(\overline{x},y^\ast)$, we have
 
$$
h(y_\lambda) \leq \gamma\lambda h(\overline{x}) + (1-\gamma\lambda)h(y^\ast) + \tfrac{\gamma\rho}{2}\lambda\Big(1-\tfrac{\lambda}{2-\gamma}\Big)\|y^\ast-\overline{x}\|^2 .
$$
 
Substituting into \eqref{eq:step21} and using $h(\overline{x})=h^{\beta}(\overline{x})$,
 
\begin{equation}\label{eq:step31}
h^{\beta}(z_\lambda) \leq \gamma\lambda h^{\beta}(\overline{x}) + (1-\gamma\lambda)h(y^\ast) + \tfrac{\gamma\rho}{2}\lambda\Big(1-\tfrac{\lambda}{2-\gamma}\Big)\|y^\ast-\overline{x}\|^2 + \tfrac{(1-\lambda)^2}{2{\beta}}\|x-y^\ast\|^2 .
\end{equation}
 
From \eqref{eq:near-opt}, $h(y^\ast)\leq h^{\beta}(x)+\varepsilon-\tfrac{1}{2{\beta}}\|x-y^\ast\|^2$. Since $1-\gamma\lambda\ge0$, substitute into \eqref{eq:step31} we get
 
\begin{align}
h^{\beta}(z_\lambda) &\leq \gamma\lambda h^{\beta}(\overline{x})+(1-\gamma\lambda)\big(h^{\beta}(x)+\varepsilon\big) + \tfrac{\gamma\rho}{2}\lambda\Big(1-\tfrac{\lambda}{2-\gamma}\Big)\|y^\ast-\overline{x}\|^2 \nonumber\\
&\qquad + \tfrac{1}{2{\beta}}\big((1-\lambda)^2-(1-\gamma\lambda)\big)\|x-y^\ast\|^2 . \label{eq:step41}
\end{align}
 
Since $(1-\lambda)^2-(1-\gamma\lambda) = -\lambda(2-\gamma-\lambda)$, $\lambda\in[0,1]$ and $\gamma \in   ]0,1]$, we have $2-\gamma-\lambda\ge1-\gamma\ge0$, this bracket is $\le0$. Let $c := \tfrac{ \gamma\rho}{2-\gamma}\ge0$, so $\tfrac{\gamma\rho}{2}\big(1-\tfrac{\lambda}{2-\gamma}\big)=\tfrac{c}{2}(2-\gamma-\lambda)$. Factor $\tfrac{\lambda(2-\gamma-\lambda)}{2}$ from the two quadratic terms in \eqref{eq:step41} gives
$$ \tfrac{c}{2}(2-\gamma-\lambda)\lambda\|y^\ast-\overline{x}\|^2 - \tfrac{\lambda(2-\gamma-\lambda)}{2{\beta}}\|x-y^\ast\|^2 = \tfrac{\lambda(2-\gamma-\lambda)}{2}\Big(c\|y^\ast-\overline{x}\|^2 - \tfrac1{\beta}\|x-y^\ast\|^2\Big).$$
 
Set $u:=y^\ast-x$ and $v:=x-\overline{x}$, so $y^\ast-\overline{x} = u+v$, and
 
$$ c \|y^\ast-\overline{x}\|^2-\tfrac1{\beta}\|x-y^\ast \|^2 = -\Big(\tfrac1{\beta}-c\Big)\|u\|^2 + 2 c\langle u,v\rangle + c\|v\|^2.$$
 
Let $A := \tfrac1{\beta} - c$. The assumption \eqref{param:cond:2} is equivalent to $c\beta<1$. Indeed, if $\rho=0$, then $c=0$, and if $\rho>0$, then $\beta<\tfrac{2-\gamma}{\gamma\rho}$ if and only if $\tfrac{\gamma\rho\beta}{2-\gamma}<1$. Hence, $A = \tfrac1\beta-c=\tfrac{1-c\beta}{\beta}>0$.

 We can maximize this quadratic form over $u$ by completing the square
\begin{align*}
 - A \|u\|^2 + 2c\langle u, v \rangle + c\|v\|^2 &= -A \left\|u - \tfrac{c}{A} v \right\|^2 + \tfrac{c^2}{A} \|v\|^2 + c\|v\|^2 \leq c \left(\tfrac{c+A}{A} \right)\|v\|^2.
\end{align*}
 
Substituting $A = \tfrac1{\beta} - c$ back into the scalar coefficient yields
$c\tfrac{(c + (\tfrac{1}{\beta} - c))}{(\tfrac{1}{\beta} - c)} = \tfrac{c}{1 - c {\beta}}$. Then, we obtain the tight upper bound
 
$$ c\|y^\ast-\overline{x}\|^2-\tfrac1{\beta}\|x-y^\ast\|^2 \leq \tfrac{c}{1-c{\beta}}\|x-\overline{x}\|^2 .$$
 
Hence,
 
$$
\tfrac{\gamma\rho}{2}\lambda\Big(1-\tfrac{\lambda}{2-\gamma}\Big)\|y^\ast-\overline{x}\|^2 - \tfrac{\lambda(2-\gamma-\lambda)}{2{\beta}}\|x-y^\ast\|^2 \leq \tfrac{\lambda(2-\gamma-\lambda)}{2}\cdot\tfrac{c}{1-c{\beta}}\|x-\overline{x}\|^2 .
$$
 
Substituting into \eqref{eq:step41} and using $\lambda(2-\gamma-\lambda)=(2-\gamma)\lambda\big(1-\tfrac{\lambda}{2-\gamma}\big)$, we have
 
\begin{align*}
 & \hspace{0.8cm} h^{\beta}(z_\lambda) \leq \gamma \lambda h^{\beta}(\overline{x})+(1-\gamma \lambda) h^{\beta}(x) + (1-\gamma \lambda) \varepsilon + \tfrac{c (2-\gamma)}{2 (1-c{\beta})}\lambda \Big(1-\tfrac{\lambda}{2-\gamma} \Big) \|x-\overline{x}\|^2 \\
 & \overset{\varepsilon \downarrow 0}{\Longrightarrow} \, h^{\beta}(z_\lambda) \leq \gamma\lambda h^{\beta}(\overline{x}) + (1-\gamma\lambda)h^{\beta}(x) + \tfrac{c(2-\gamma)}{2(1-c{\beta})}\lambda\Big(1-\tfrac{\lambda}{2-\gamma}\Big)\|x-\overline{x}\|^2 .
\end{align*}
Comparing with \eqref{eq:quasar-wconvex}, this is the $(\rho_{\beta},\gamma)$-weak quasar-convexity inequality for $h^{\beta}$, with
 
$$
\tfrac{\gamma\rho_{\beta}}{2} = \tfrac{c(2-\gamma)}{2(1-c{\beta})} \iff \rho_{\beta} = \tfrac{(2-\gamma)c}{\gamma(1-c{\beta})} = \tfrac{\rho}{1-c{\beta}},
$$
 
using $c = \tfrac{\gamma \rho}{2-\gamma}$. This is exactly \eqref{eq:rho-mu}. Since $x\in\mathbb{R}^n$ and $\lambda \in [0,1]$ were arbitrary, the proof is complete.

label: rem:beta-range
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rem:beta-range}
Let $\rho\ge 0$ and $\gamma \in ]0,1]$, with the convention that both $\tfrac{1}{\rho}$ and $\tfrac{2-\gamma}{\gamma \rho}$ equal $+\infty$ when $\rho=0$.
Since $\gamma \leq 2-\gamma$, it holds that
\[
 \tfrac{1}{\rho} \leq \tfrac{2-\gamma}{\gamma\rho},
\]
with equality if and only if $\gamma=1$ (or $\rho=0$). Consequently, Theorem~\ref{prop:moreau-structural} applies in particular for every $0< \beta <\tfrac{1}{\rho}$, and the same conclusion remains valid. In this range, the relation $c= \tfrac{\gamma\rho}{2-\gamma} \le \rho$ yields the simpler (yet weaker) upper bound
\[
 \rho_{\beta} = \tfrac{\rho}{1-c\beta} \leq \tfrac{ \rho}{1-\rho\beta}.
\]
Condition \eqref{param:cond:2} is precisely the requirement needed in the proof, namely $A=\tfrac{1}{\beta}-c>0$.
\qed

label: prox:nonempty
title: Corollary
body_md:
\label{prox:nonempty}
Let $\mathcal{K}\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n$ be a nonempty closed convex set and let $h:\mathbb{R}^n\to\overline{\mathbb{R}}$ be proper and
lower semicontinuous, with $\mathcal{K}\cap\operatorname{dom}(h)\neq\emptyset$ and $\overline{x}\in\operatorname{argmin}_{\mathcal{K}} h$. Then, for every
$\beta>0$ and every $x\in\mathbb{R}^n$, the set $\operatorname{Prox}_{\beta h}(\mathcal{K},x)$ is nonempty and compact. In particular,
this holds for every $(\rho,\gamma)$-weakly quasar-convex function with respect to $\overline{x}$,
without any restriction on $\beta$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md: For every $y\in \mathcal{K}$ we have $h(y)\ge h(\overline{x})$, hence $h(y)+\tfrac{1}{2\beta} \|x-y\|^2 \ge h(\overline{x})+\tfrac{1}{2\beta}\|x-y\|^2$, exactly as in Lemma \ref{coercivity:2}. Thus $\Phi:=h+\iota_{\mathcal{K}}+\tfrac{1}{2\beta}\|x-\cdot\|^2$ is proper, lower semicontinuous and coercive, so its set of minimizers is nonempty and compact.

label: exam:qg-application
title: Example
body_md:
\label{exam:qg-application}
Let $f(s)=2-\sqrt{|s|}$ be as in Example~\ref{exam:large}, and let $\varphi$ be the function of Example~\ref{exam:qg-radial}. Divide $\mathbb{R}^2$ into the four closed regions delimited by the lines $x_2=x_1$ and $x_2=-x_1$, namely
\begin{align*}
\mathcal{A} &:= \left\{(x_1,x_2)\in\mathbb{R}^2:~ x_1 \geq 0,  -x_1 \leq x_2 \leq x_1\right\}, &
\mathcal{B} &:= \left\{(x_1,x_2)\in\mathbb{R}^2:~ x_2 \geq 0,  -x_2 \leq x_1 \leq x_2\right\}, \\
\mathcal{C} &:= \left\{(x_1,x_2)\in\mathbb{R}^2:~ x_1 \leq 0,  x_1 \leq x_2 \leq -x_1\right\}, &
\mathcal{D} &:= \left\{(x_1,x_2)\in\mathbb{R}^2:~ x_2 \leq 0,  x_2 \leq x_1 \leq -x_2\right\}.
\end{align*}
Define $H:\mathbb{R}^2\to\mathbb{R}$ by $H(0,0):=0$, and for $(x_1,x_2)\neq(0,0)$,
\begin{equation*}
H(x_1,x_2) :=
\begin{cases}
\varphi(x_1)~ f\!\left(\dfrac{x_2}{x_1}\right), & (x_1,x_2) \in \mathcal{A}, \\[3mm]
\varphi(x_2)~ f\!\left(\dfrac{x_1}{x_2}\right), & (x_1,x_2) \in \mathcal{B}, \\[3mm]
\varphi(-x_1)~ f\!\left(\dfrac{x_2}{-x_1}\right), & (x_1,x_2) \in \mathcal{C}, \\[3mm]
\varphi(-x_2)~ f\!\left(\dfrac{x_1}{-x_2}\right), & (x_1,x_2) \in \mathcal{D}.
\end{cases}
\end{equation*}
The four formulas agree on the shared boundary rays $x_2=\pm x_1$, so $H$ is well defined and continuous on $\mathbb{R}^2$.

\medskip
\noindent
\emph{Unique global minimizer.} Since $\varphi(s)=0$ if and only if $s=0$ by Example~\ref{exam:qg-radial}$(i)$ and $f>0$ on $[-1,1]$, the same argument as in Example~\ref{exam:large} shows $H(x)=0$ if and only if $x=(0,0)$, thus $\{(0,0)\}=\operatorname{argmin}_{\mathbb{R}^2}H$.

\medskip
\noindent
\emph{Local quadratic growth with $\mu_H=1$.} On $\mathcal{A}$, using $\varphi(t)=t^2$ for $t\in[0,1]$ and $f\geq1$, we have
\begin{equation*}
 H(x_1,x_2) = \varphi(x_1) f\!\left( \frac{x_2}{x_1} \right) \geq \varphi(x_1) \geq x_1^2 \geq \frac12 \|x\|^2, \qquad \forall  (x_1, x_2) \in \mathcal{A},\ 0< x_1 \leq 1,
\end{equation*}
using $|x_2|\leq x_1$ on $\mathcal{A}$. The same bound holds trivially at $(0,0)$. On the other hand, for every $(x_1,x_2)\in \mathcal{A}$ with $x_1 \ge 1$ we have $H(x_1,x_2) \ge \varphi(x_1) \ge 1$, by Example \ref{exam:qg-radial}(iii) and $f\ge1$. Hence, for every $\zeta \in \, ]0, 1[$, the sublevel set $\{H \le \zeta\} \cap \mathcal{A}$ is contained in $\{x_1 < 1\}$, where the bound above holds.

\medskip
\noindent
\emph{Weak quasar-convexity with $\rho_H = \tfrac12$.} On any ray through the origin, $x_2/x_1 = c \in [-1,1]$ constant, so restricted to that ray, $H(t,ct) = f(c) \varphi(t)$ is a positive scalar multiple of $\varphi$, with $f(c) \in [1,2]$. Since $\varphi$ is $\tfrac14$-weakly convex on $\mathbb{R}$ by Example \ref{exam:qg-radial}$(ii)$, multiplying by $f(c)\leq2$ gives that $t \mapsto f(c) \varphi(t)$ is $\tfrac12$-weakly convex, hence $\left(\tfrac12, 1\right)$-weakly quasar-convex with respect to $t=0$, for every $c \in [-1, 1]$. As in Example~\ref{exam:large}$(i)$, this shows $H$ is $\left(\tfrac12, 1\right)$-weakly quasar-convex with respect to $(0, 0)$ on $\mathbb{R}^2$.

\medskip
\noindent
\emph{Not weakly convex for any modulus.} Fix $\rho\geq0$ and, for $s\in ]0,1]$, consider $(1,-s),(1,s)\in\mathbb{R}^2$ and their midpoint $(1,0)$. Since $f$ is even, $H(1,\pm s)=\varphi(1)f(s)$ and $H(1,0)=\varphi(1)f(0)$. As in Example~\ref{exam:large}$(ii)$, weak convexity with modulus $\rho$ would require $\varphi(1)\sqrt{s}\leq\tfrac\rho2 s^2$, using $\varphi(1)=1>0$ and $f(0)-f(s)=\sqrt s$; this fails as $s\to0^+$ for any fixed $\rho\geq0$. Hence, $H$ is not weakly convex on $\mathbb{R}^2$ for any modulus.

\medskip
\noindent
\emph{Neither (star) quasi-convexity nor $\gamma$-quasar-convexity for any $\gamma\in ]0,1]$}. It suffices to consider $H$ restricted to $(t,0)$, $t\geq0$, where $H(t,0)=f(0)\varphi(t)=2\varphi(t)$. Using Example~\ref{exam:qg-radial}$(iv)$--$(v)$, we get
\begin{equation*}
 H(0,0)=0, \qquad H(9,0)=18, \qquad H(13.5,0) = \frac{27}{2}.
\end{equation*}
Since $H (9,0) = 18 > \tfrac{27}{2} = \max\{H(0,0), H(13.5,0)\}$, and $(9,0)$ lies on the segment joining $(0,0)$ and $(13.5,0)$, this violates quasi-convexity and star quasi-convexity with respect to $(0,0)$ (see \cite[Theorem 12]{PQK-L}). Furthermore, taking $x=(13.5,0)$, $\lambda = \tfrac13$, the same computation as in Example \ref{exam:qg-radial}$(v)$ (scaled by the common factor $2$) shows $H(9,0)=18 > \left(1-\tfrac\gamma3 \right)\cdot\tfrac{27}{2}$ for every $\gamma \in   ]0,1]$, so $H$ is not $\gamma$-quasar-convex with respect to $(0,0)$, for any $\gamma \in   ]0,1]$.

\medskip

Therefore, $H$ is $\left(\tfrac12,1\right)$-weakly quasar-convex with respect to its unique global minimizer $\overline{x}=(0,0)$, and satisfies the $1$-local quadratic growth condition \eqref{eq:QG} at $\overline{x}$ for every $\zeta \in ]0, 1[$, with
\begin{equation*}
 \mu_H = 1  >  \tfrac12 = \rho_H,
\end{equation*}
yet $H$ is neither weakly convex, nor quasi-convex, nor star quasi-convex, nor quasar-convex, for any modulus. As a consequence, provided the initial point $x^0$ of the PPM satisfies $H(x^0)<1$ (so that the trajectory remains within the region of validity $\zeta \in ]0, 1[$), Theorem~\ref{thm:ppm-linear} applies to $H$, while no other result in the literature does.
\qed
